title: Center-of-mass squared norm
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. The sum of the squares of the coordinates of the small-set center of mass of $f$ at scale $\alpha$ equals the level-one Fourier weight of $f$ divided by $\alpha^2$. At $\alpha=0$, both sides are zero under the usual totalized real division convention.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube of dimension $n$
